On the latest narrative fair value, Colgate-Palmolive at $99.67 trades above an estimated $86.48, which raises a clear pricing question according to rcb9, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who built that valuation framework.

"This creates a trap worth naming. If you normalise the margin but leave the future multiple at the GAAP-derived figure, you count the adjustment twice and overstate fair value by roughly 45%. The margin and the multiple have to sit on the same basis. That is why 15% pairs with 24x here rather than with 35x."

The valuation work from rcb9 rests on a few core inputs. Those assumptions tie closely to Colgate-Palmolive guidance and recent margin history in the narrative, and they sit below the current analyst price target of $101.70 even before layering in any extra optimism.

Readers get a helpful warning here about mixing metrics that do not share the same base. The narrative argues that reported net margin around 10% is distorted by a one off impairment, while a normalised level near the mid teens lines up with cash generation and prior years. If you lift earnings to that higher margin yet keep using a P/E multiple built off compressed GAAP results, you are effectively rewarding the adjustment twice in your spreadsheet.

On that logic, the narrative sees Colgate-Palmolive as a high quality consumer staples group with a strong oral care position, but one where a lot of that quality is already embedded in the share price. The gap between $99.67 and $86.48 is not framed as a bubble. It is presented as a 15.3% premium that relies on what the author describes as "competent continuation" in categories like toothpaste and pet nutrition rather than any radical shift.

Still, this fair value gap could close quickly if North America keeps lagging or if another impairment charge signals deeper trouble in Colgate-Palmolive’s skin health portfolio.
